title: Graphing the Absolute Value of a Quadratic Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = |x^2 - 1| by writing it in piecewise form and describing how it is obtained from the parabola y = x^2 - 1.

steps.title: Express y = |x^2 - 1| in Piecewise Form
steps.mathExpression: y = |x^2 - 1| = \begin{cases} x^2 - 1, & x \le -1 \text{ or } x \ge 1 \\ -(x^2 - 1) = 1 - x^2, & -1 < x < 1 \end{cases}
steps.explanation: The inner parabola x^2 - 1 is non-negative on (-infinity, -1] U [1, infinity) and negative on (-1, 1). Applying the absolute value leaves the outer branches unchanged and reflects the portion below the x-axis on (-1, 1) across the x-axis.
steps.why: By definition of absolute value, |u| = u when u >= 0 and |u| = -u when u < 0.

steps.title: Identify the Domain, Range, and Symmetry
steps.explanation: The function is defined for all real x, is symmetric about the y-axis, and has range [0, infinity).
steps.why: Taking the absolute value of a continuous function that crosses zero yields minimum value 0.

steps.title: Locate Corners, Intercepts, and Local Extrema
steps.explanation: Reflecting the vertex (0, -1) of y = x^2 - 1 across the x-axis creates a local maximum arch peaking at (0, 1), meeting the upward outer parabolic branches at sharp corners at (-1, 0) and (1, 0).
steps.why: Where x^2 - 1 changes sign transversely at x = +/-1, |x^2 - 1| has sharp corners with opposite one-sided slopes.
